name: Sweet Potato Chaat
steps: Scrub the sweet potatoes and rinse off all soil. Place them whole in a heavy covered pan over low heat, without oil, using similarly sized roots so they roast evenly.

Cook for 35–45 minutes, turning every 6–8 minutes with tongs. The skins may blister; lower the heat if they scorch quickly. Test the thickest part with a skewer: it should pass through without resistance.
While the sweet potatoes cook, toast the cumin in a small dry pan for about 1 minute until fragrant. Cool briefly and crush with the black pepper. Finely chop the coriander.
Rest the cooked sweet potatoes off the heat for 5 minutes. Peel carefully while warm and remove any charred skin; cut the soft flesh into bite-sized chunks.
Place the chunks in a bowl and sprinkle with the crushed spices and rock salt. Add lemon juice and turn gently so the pieces are seasoned without being mashed.
Finish with coriander and serve warm. Taste a piece before serving; the lemon should balance the natural sweetness without pooling at the bottom.
tips: This fasting-style version uses rock salt and freshly toasted cumin rather than a mixed chaat masala.
passiveTime: Rest roasted sweet potatoes for 5 minutes before peeling.
notes: Four adult portions. Listed time covers preparation and cooking; additional soaking, cooling or resting is stated separately. Fasting customs vary: check every ingredient against your household practice. Jain suitability depends on your saved ingredient rules.
